market_name: Will the U.S. invade Iran before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket probability move is sustained or a thin-liquidity blip; cross-check Brent/WTI futures and any Reuters/Bloomberg headlines on US-Iran posture.
time_plan.1h: Confirm oil futures direction, watch tanker-tracking and Hormuz shipping chatter, and whether official statements (White House, CENTCOM) corroborate escalation.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether the move is spreading to gold and defense names (confirmation of a genuine risk-on-conflict regime) versus isolated noise.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether the oil premium is holding or fading; check for official denials that would reverse the premium.
time_plan.12h: Measure realized USO move versus the 700bps tradable threshold; note whether the prediction-market signal led or lagged public news.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp upward repricing in the probability of a US invasion of Iran signals rising escalation risk in the Persian Gulf, which threatens roughly a fifth of global seaborne oil throughput (Strait of Hormuz). Markets price a geopolitical risk premium into crude almost immediately on credible conflict escalation. USO is a liquid, directly exposed proxy. Magnitude depends heavily on how large and credible the implied-probability move is; a decisive jump could produce a double-digit-percent spike, a modest drift much less.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify the probability move is real and durable, not a liquidity artifact; check spot gold and DXY simultaneously.
time_plan.1h: Watch whether Treasuries and gold rally together (genuine haven bid) versus a dollar-led move that could cap gold.
time_plan.2h: Confirm cross-asset coherence: oil up + equities down + gold up would validate the escalation regime.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether haven bid persists or mean-reverts on any de-escalation headlines.
time_plan.12h: Compare realized GLD move to expectation; likely below the 700bps tradable threshold, so treat as confirming signal rather than standalone trade.

predictions.reasoning: Rising probability of a major US military offensive against Iran is a classic safe-haven catalyst: gold tends to bid on war-risk escalation alongside a flight from risk assets. GLD is a highly liquid proxy. The move is typically smaller and noisier than oil's, and can be offset if a risk-off dollar rally dominates, so confidence and magnitude are lower.

evidence_used: Market question implies escalation risk of direct US military action against Iran
Iran/Persian Gulf proximity to Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil chokepoint
Historical pattern: geopolitical conflict escalation lifts crude and gold, pressures broad equities
Liquidity of USO and GLD as broadly traded proxies
uncertainty_notes: This card is pre-commitment; it does not assume the probability actually moved — it maps what WOULD move if it did
Prediction markets are noisy and thin; a probability jump may reflect low-liquidity speculation rather than leaked information
Magnitude is highly sensitive to the size and credibility of the implied-probability change
If the escalation were already public (news-driven), the asset move may already be priced and reverse

llm_justification.summary: A sharp upward move in the implied probability of a US invasion of Iran maps most directly to a higher oil risk premium (USO up) via Strait of Hormuz supply-disruption fears, and secondarily to a safe-haven bid in gold (GLD up). Crude is the strongest, most liquid proxy and could plausibly exceed the 700bps tradable threshold on a decisive, credible repricing; gold is a weaker, noisier confirming signal. Both depend on the probability move being genuine and not already public.
key_assumptions: The prediction-market probability moved sharply and credibly, not as thin-market noise
Escalation risk is not already fully priced into oil and gold
Strait of Hormuz / Gulf supply disruption remains the dominant transmission channel
No simultaneous offsetting macro shock (e.g., demand collapse) dominates oil
failure_modes: The probability spike is a liquidity artifact or speculative blip that reverses, taking any asset move with it
The escalation is already public via headlines, so oil/gold have already moved and mean-revert within the window
A dollar-led risk-off move offsets the gold haven bid, flattening GLD
Oil fails to react if markets judge the invasion probability still too low to warrant a sustained premium
US-Iran de-escalation or official denial reverses the premium quickly
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
